gaps.sentence: When I was a student, I used ___ in shared flats.
gaps.explanation: used TO + infinitive = past habit/state: used to live. (Compare: be used to living.)

gaps.sentence: I didn't mean ___ you — it was a joke.
gaps.explanation: mean (= intend) takes the to-infinitive: didn't mean to upset. (mean + -ing = involve.)

gaps.sentence: I can't imagine ___ in a tiny village again.
I look forward to ___ you at the reunion.
gaps.explanation: 'To' is a preposition here, so the gerund follows.

gaps.sentence: I can't afford ___ another month abroad.
I want you ___ the truth, whatever it is.
gaps.explanation: want + object + to-infinitive: want you to tell.

gaps.sentence: Would you mind ___ the window? It's boiling in here.
gaps.explanation: mind is followed by -ing: Would you mind opening…?

gaps.sentence: My parents wouldn't let me ___ out that late.
gaps.explanation: let takes the bare infinitive: let me go (no 'to').
